answer: Each identity must solve a memory-hard puzzle bound to its own trade history before trading each epoch. The puzzle input includes the hash of its last settled deal, so solutions cannot be shared or precomputed for new keys. One honest agent spends a few seconds of memory bandwidth and enters the harbor of active traders. A sybil farmer faces a canyon of parallel memory demand: a thousand fakes need a thousand distinct puzzle runs, each as hard as carving marble, so cloning keys multiplies hardware cost instead of influence.
